limiting_points.suggested_action: Compare the PC-tile architecture and folding pathway directly with the closest RNA paranemic-crossover, single-stranded origami, and cellular co-transcriptional systems, separating architectural precedent from the cellular TEM demonstration.
limiting_points.text: The paper identifies closely related parallel-crossover, single-stranded origami, and co-transcriptional RNA work. The extent to which the architectural design itself, rather than the direct nuclear TEM visualization, is distinct from these precedents requires external comparison.

supporting_points.suggested_action: Frame the central advance as the demonstrated co-transcriptional formation and direct structural visualization of defined RNA nanonets in human cell nuclei.
supporting_points.text: The contribution is a programmable single-stranded RNA system that forms defined assemblies co-transcriptionally and is structurally visualized in human cells by both cellular imaging and TEM.

questions.suggested_action: Test structural, sequence, and trafficking-factor perturbations that can distinguish retention from export and establish whether localization can be predictably controlled.
questions.text: Which structural and cellular factors determine nuclear retention versus cytosolic distribution, and can a defined design change reproducibly switch the localization outcome?

questions.suggested_action: Evaluate cellular assembly and localization across smaller, linear, and additional two-dimensional designs using the same quantitative analysis applied to D4 and D10.
questions.text: Do cellular assembly and nuclear enrichment extend beyond the two large nanonet designs D4 and D10 to smaller or linear RNA tile architectures?

strengths.suggested_action: Retain the explicit link between the PC/KL design choices, the programmed geometries, and the co-transcriptional AFM characterization.
strengths.text: The work supplies a design framework using paranemic cohesion and kissing-loop interactions to program co-transcriptionally folded rings, linear arrays, and two-dimensional lattices, with AFM characterization of multiple architectures.

strengths.suggested_action: Preserve the quantitative distribution analysis and the orthogonal AFM, cellular-imaging, and TEM comparison for the tested D4 and D10 assemblies.
strengths.text: For D4 and D10, the study combines cellular imaging with TEM and compares periodic features to AFM reference structures, providing convergent evidence for assembled nanonet-like structures in transfected human cells.

summary.text: This study develops single-stranded RNA tiles that fold co-transcriptionally through paranemic cohesion and kissing-loop interactions, assemble into programmed architectures, and are examined in human cells. The evidence supports the design framework and, for D4 and D10, convergent cellular-imaging and TEM evidence of nanonet-like assemblies. The remaining scope limits are that localization is not exclusively nuclear, its mechanism remains unresolved, and in-cell evaluation is confined to two large designs. Novelty is strongest for the direct cellular structural visualization, whereas the architectural distinction from close RNA crossover and origami precedents requires explicit comparison.

weaknesses.suggested_action: Constrain localization claims to the measured distributions of D4 and D10 and distinguish observed nuclear enrichment from a demonstrated, general mechanism of nuclear retention.
weaknesses.text: The inference of a preferred nuclear localization should be qualified: both tested designs include cells with nucleus-and-cytosol distributions, and the paper states that the factors governing localization and retention remain to be determined.
